# `launch-window`

Scenario kind of the engine v0.38.0, family [Mission analysis, links and space operations](../mission-analysis-links-and-space-operations.md). Advisory: analysis output from a research and engineering tool, not type-approved navigation equipment and not a safety-of-life service. Every label here is the engine's or the verification matrix's; a kind is MODELLED unless the matrix says otherwise (how a label is earned: the README's Evidence section).

## What it does

Two-body launch & ascent geometry: launch azimuth(s) (sin Az = cos i / cos lat), minimum reachable inclination, circular velocity, the Earth-rotation eastward bonus, dogleg plane-change Δv when the target inclination is below the site latitude, and the number of daily launch opportunities. MODELLED spherical-Earth geometry (no rotating-Earth velocity-triangle correction, no ascent/drag-loss model).

One run of `scenarios/launch-window.toml` summarises as: launch-window: lat 28.5° -> i 51.6°: Az 45.0° asc, v_circ 7669 m/s, +409 m/s Earth-rotation bonus, 2 opportunities/day (MODELLED)

## Inputs

From the schema (`kshana kinds --json`):

- Required fields: none
- Optional fields: `site_lat_deg`, `target_inclination_deg`, `altitude_km`, `site_lon_deg`, `epoch`, `eop_finals2000a`

The example `scenarios/launch-window.toml` sets, among others:

| Field | Value | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| `altitude_km` | 400 | km |
| `kind` | launch-window | text |
| `site_lat_deg` | 28.5 | deg |
| `target_inclination_deg` | 51.6 | deg |

## Run it

```sh
kshana scenarios/launch-window.toml
```
